subject: Annualized Upfront Quote & Exit Mechanics for Crestwell Health
messages:
From: Emma Li <emma@crestwell.io>
To: karthik_iyer@redwood.com, procurement@crestwell.io
Date: Tue, 10 Nov 2026 09:12:00 -0800
Subject: Question on multi-year upfront pricing and cancellation

Hi Karthik,

Thanks for the demo last week — our execs liked the latency and cost story. Before we pull procurement into the formal review, two quick clarifications on the multi-year upfront offer you sent:

1) Refund mechanics: If Crestwell needs to scale down or terminate year 2, what does the refund look like for the unused portion of the prepay? Is it prorated, amortized, or subject to a termination credit schedule?
2) Ramp schedule and discounts: The spreadsheet shows a 20% annual discount for a 3-year commit with a 12/6/6 ramp. Can you confirm how the discount applies if we front-load more in year 1?
3) Co-terming: We have existing contracts with a different vendor that co-term in Oct 2027 — will there be any penalty to align with our other contracts?

We want to understand the economic exposure so we can brief finance and legal. If you have a short matrix or simple examples, that would be really helpful.

Thanks,
Emma Li
Director, Cloud Ops
Crestwell Health


From: karthik_iyer@redwood.com
To: Emma Li <emma@crestwell.io>
Cc: lauren_bishop@redwood.com, vivek_kulkarni@redwood.com
Date: Wed, 11 Nov 2026 10:03:00 -0800
Subject: Re: Question on multi-year upfront pricing and cancellation

Emma — thanks for the clear list. High-level answers below; attaching a one-page amortization + exit matrix and a sample quote that shows two variants (front-loaded year1 vs evenly amortized).

Summary (short):
- Refund approach: Redwood offers an early termination credit schedule for prepay contracts. We amortize the committed prepay over the contracted term to calculate remaining value, then apply an early termination processing fee (standard = 10% of remaining unamortized value) unless a negotiated exception is included.
- Front-loading: If you front-load spend in year 1 we can show two models: (A) counted as prepay applied to consumption first with annual discount applied to the contracted commitment; (B) your company can elect accelerated recognition (higher discount year1) but that reduces discount headroom in later years.
- Co-terming: Aligning term dates is doable; we can either a) provide a pro-rata true-up at the co-term date or b) re-amortize remaining unused prepay into a co-term bridge with a small processing fee.

Attachments: RI_AnnualizedQuote_Crestwell_v1.xlsx (spreadsheet - contains amortization examples), termination_refund_matrix.csv (CSV - line-item examples)

Proposed next steps:
- I can run two concrete scenarios for you (front-loaded vs straight-line) and send a redline-friendly termination paragraph for legal to review. Can your procurement lead confirm a good time for a 30-min call?

Thanks,

Subject: Internal: Need quick legal + finance take on Crestwell termination wording

Hey team — forwarding Crestwell's two asks. I attached the two example files (amortization + matrix). Can you please:

- Lauren: propose a termination clause that preserves customer-first refunds but limits upstream exposure (we expect CLTV ~3x prepay in most cases). Keep processing fee at 10% as a baseline, but be explicit about what counts as "unused" (unbilled credits vs reserved capacity).
- Vivek: sanity-check the numbers — specifically confirm that the 10% processing fee + straight-line amortization produces acceptable revenue recognition outcomes for us and doesn't create a large clawback risk if they accelerate year1.

Time sensitive — procurement wants a revised paragraph by Monday.

Thanks,
Karthik


From: lauren_bishop@redwood.com
To: karthik_iyer@redwood.com, Emma Li <emma@crestwell.io>
Cc: vivek_kulkarni@redwood.com
Date: Mon, 16 Nov 2026 09:15:00 -0800
Subject: Re: Annualized Upfront Quote & Exit Mechanics for Crestwell Health

Emma and team — looping in our legal perspective inline. I attached a short doc (Legal_termination_suggestion_20261113.docx) with suggested language; key points below.

Suggested termination paragraph (plain language):
- Upon Customer-initiated termination of the Agreement prior to the end of the Term, Redwood will calculate the unamortized portion of Customer's prepaid fees as of the effective termination date, refund such unamortized amount less a termination processing fee equal to ten percent (10%). Unamortized fees are calculated by straight-line amortization over the contracted term, applied to the invoiced prepaid amount.
- Exceptions: No refunds for any portion of prepaid fees that have already been used to procure committed or reserved capacity where third-party cancellation penalties would apply.
- Co-terming option: At Customer request, Redwood will offer a co-term true-up: unamortized prepaid fees may be re-amortized over the co-term period in lieu of immediate refund, subject to a re-amortization fee of 5%.

A couple of clarifications for finance (Vivek):
- We should define "effective termination date" precisely and give Redwood 30 days to process refunds or offer re-amortization.
- If Crestwell elects re-amortization to align co-terms, they must sign an amendment documenting the new schedule.

If this aligns with your risk appetite, we can insert the paragraph into the SOW and send to procurement for confirmation. Happy to tighten language if procurement/legal asks for more specificity.

Best,
Lauren Bishop
Senior Counsel | Redwood Inference
lauren_bishop@redwood.com

Emma — thanks for the patience. Based on your note and our counsel's language below, suggested commercial path we discussed on the call:

1) Option A (standard): 3-year prepaid (USD) with straight-line amortization. Early termination refund = unamortized balance minus 10% processing fee.
2) Option B (front-loaded): Year1 prepay increase + matched discount (one-time additional 5% on year1 only). Early termination still uses straight-line amortization; the upfront additional discount is treated as accelerated recognition and not refundable if used.
3) Co-terming: We can offer re-amortization into your Oct 2027 co-term with a 5% re-amortization fee (no immediate cash refund).

Next steps:
- I'll attach the DocuSign with Option A prepopulated. If you'd like Option B, please reply and I'll update numbers and re-send.
- Procurement: if you want more examples I can send a 2x scenario file.
